title: Semicon 2.0 and Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme
text:
The Union Cabinet on 15 July 2026 approved seven decisions with a combined outlay of about ₹2.19 lakh crore. Two electronics schemes made up most of that amount.

The first is Semicon 2.0, the second phase of the India Semiconductor Mission, with an outlay of ₹1,27,500 crore. The government expects it to draw about ₹4 lakh crore in investment and to support semiconductor production worth ₹2 lakh crore during the scheme period. Its six focus areas are chip design, equipment and materials, new fabs, assembly and packaging, research and development, and talent. Support therefore extends beyond chip fabrication.

The second is the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme, with a budgetary outlay of ₹62,500 crore for FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31. It has two target segments: manufacturing in India, and Indian mobile phone brands. Its aim is to scale up domestic mobile phone production.

Together, the two schemes come to about ₹1.9 lakh crore. The same meeting also cleared highway projects and urea plant decisions.

questions.q: What was the initial outlay of the first phase of the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM 1.0), approved by the Union Cabinet?
questions.explanation: The Union Cabinet approved ISM 1.0 with an initial outlay of ₹76,000 crore. The ₹65,000 crore figure is only the allocation for chip fabrication and packaging units within that package, and ₹10,000 crore was set aside for the Mohali lab.

questions.q: Under Article 280 of the Constitution, the Finance Commission is constituted by the President at the expiration of every how many years, unless an earlier time is considered necessary?
questions.explanation: Article 280 requires the President to constitute a Finance Commission at the expiry of every fifth year, or earlier if the President considers it necessary.

questions.q: Which ministry administers the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS)?
options: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
questions.explanation: The MPMS is a Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) scheme. The other three ministries do not administer it.

Article 112 provides for the Annual Financial Statement (the Budget); Article 266 creates the Consolidated Fund of India; Article 267 creates the Contingency Fund of India; Article 148 provides for the Comptroller and Auditor General.

questions.assertion: The first phase of the India Semiconductor Mission was approved by the Union Cabinet in December 2021.
questions.reason: The India Semiconductor Mission functions under the Ministry of Finance.
questions.explanation: The assertion is true: the Cabinet approved the ISM 1.0 package on 15 December 2021. The reason is false: the ISM is run under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), not the Ministry of Finance.

statements: I. Under Article 75(3), the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
II. A Money Bill may be returned by the Rajya Sabha with its recommendations within a period of fourteen days.
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. Article 75(3) makes the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. Under Article 109, the Rajya Sabha has up to fourteen days to return a Money Bill with recommendations.

statements: 1. Manufacturers earn incentives of 2.25% to 5% on eligible sales of mobile phones manufactured in India under the MPMS.
2. The MPMS reserves an additional 3% incentive on eligible sales for design and R&D by Indian mobile phone brands.
4. The Rs 62,500 crore budgetary outlay of the MPMS excludes administrative charges.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the incentive band is 2.25% to 5% of eligible sales, and a further 3% is reserved for Indian brands' design and R&D. Statement 3 is wrong: the scheme was notified in August 2026. Statement 4 is wrong: the Rs 62,500 crore outlay includes administrative charges. Two statements are correct, so the answer is 'Only two'.

statements: I. Article 265 provides that no tax may be levied or collected except by authority of law.
II. Article 265 allows a tax to be collected on the strength of executive circulars alone.
III. Under Article 74(1), the President must act in accordance with the advice of the Council of Ministers, subject to the proviso on reconsideration.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: Article 265 requires legal authority for any tax. Statement II is wrong: executive circulars are not enough, and collection must rest on law. Statement III is correct: Article 74(1) binds the President to the Council of Ministers' advice. So 'I and III only' is the answer.

writer_flags: Passage is about 175 words, below the 220-word floor: no further facts were double-sourced within the search budget (about 11 of 20 searches used).
'Urea plant decisions' appears only in press headlines (Vajiram and Free Press Journal); amounts not stated, so kept vague.
Semicon 2.0 investment (~Rs 4 lakh crore) and production (~Rs 2 lakh crore) figures appear consistently in press summaries but the official PIB release was not opened.
Semicon 2.0 six focus areas come from search summaries and secondary explainers, not the official text.
MPMS administered by MeitY: from search summaries of superkalam, sahi and motilal; pages not opened in full.
MPMS statement 3 (not notified in 2019): notification date 21 Aug 2026 is reported by several summaries but the Gazette was not checked.
MPMS incentive band 2.25-5% and 3% for Indian-brand design/R&D: from sahi/motilal/corpseed summaries; the 3% R&D figure is secondary.
ISM 1.0 Rs 76,000 crore and 15 Dec 2021 Cabinet approval: Tribune and Powersys only; the 'run under MeitY' detail (basis of the false reason in the assertion_reason item) rests on Powersys alone.
Article 267 Contingency Fund attribution: single budget-document source, not double-sourced.
Article 266 Consolidated Fund: budget document and Lexibal, both secondary for the constitutional text.
Article 148 CAG functions: Lotus Arise and Careers360 explainers, not constitutionofindia.net (fetch failed).
Article 109 fourteen-day Rajya Sabha return: sourced only to MCQ and explainer sites, not the constitutional text.
Articles 74(1) and 75(3): sourced to explainer sites (Studyhub, Writinglaw, Careers360, PMFIAS), not the constitutional text.
Article 265 'executive circulars alone' is false by the text of the Article; the secondary summary confirms it, but this is a textual inference.
